title: Precision & Actionability Contract for Optimize Quality Gates
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Purpose: Define a compact, actionable PRD-level contract for Optimize guardrails: how we build prompt sets, what regression thresholds we accept, the statistical rules for A/B tests, and explicit rollback triggers. Goal is to make every Optimize eval produce a deterministic pass/fail recommendation and a human action list (rollback, degrade, accept, or staged ramp).

Scope: This ticket covers the evaluation gating rules used by Optimize for model/quantization/param changes that will be rolled to production or to Dedicated capacity. It covers: prompt set design, cohort sampling, primary/secondary/safety signals, decision thresholds, statistical test formalism, canary traffic windows, cost/latency constraints, and the operational runbook for failures.

Non-goals: This is not a full instrumentation implementation. It defines the contract and acceptance criteria; engineering will implement metrics and dashboards in subsequent tickets.

Assumptions:
- Optimize has existing labelled promptset sources (customer prompt samples, synthetic prompts, in-house benchmark library).
- We have telemetry for token counts, latencies (p50/p95), cost per request, and safety labels produced by the safety pipeline.
- Rollouts are done via canary routes with 1->10->50->100% traffic ramps.
acceptance_criteria: Primary metric must be defined and pre-registered before test start (examples: end-to-end task accuracy, human agreement score, or NDCG for reranking)

At least one safety metric must be tracked for every eval (hallucination_rate, toxic_content_rate, policy_violations). Any safety metric increase >0.10 percentage points (absolute) triggers immediate manual hold and automatic fail if >0.25 pp.

Minimum sample size for canary stage: 1,000 prompt interactions per cohort per model variant. For high-variance tasks the PM may require 2,500+. If sample minimums are not met, test is Inconclusive and cannot be promoted.

Primary regression threshold: absolute degradation >= 0.75 percentage points OR relative degradation >= 1.5% (whichever is larger) is considered a failing regression for primary metrics unless pre-agreed otherwise.
Secondary/performance thresholds: latency p95 increase >50ms OR relative p95 increase >25% is a fail if accompanied by no >1% improvement in primary metric; otherwise requires manual review.

Cost guardrail: cost per token/request increase >10% must be justified by >=1.5% primary improvement; otherwise fail. For Dedicated customers, use cost-per-1000-token baseline tied to committed units.

Statistical significance: primary metric decisions require a two-sided test with alpha=0.01 and sequential testing (alpha spending) for multi-window canaries. Multiple primary cohorts use Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at q=0.05.
A/B decision must include effect size (absolute and relative), p-value, confidence interval, and minimum detectable effect (MDE) calculation attached to the eval output.
Automated gate outputs must include a short human-readable reason (pass/fail/hold), the top signals that drove the decision, and the next-step recommendation (rollback/manual review/staged ramp).
All eval runs must produce a canonical artifact saved to Optimize artifacts (Confluence/GDrive link) and a GitHub PR template prefilled for any follow-up changes if the test fails.
Security review required flag must be set for any eval touching private deployments or KMS/HSM integrations.
sampling_plan: Cohorts: production-like prompt distribution split into: Broad (random sample from production traces), Safety-heavy (prompts flagged historically), Edge-cases (low-frequency but high-business-impact prompts). Stratify by customer tier (hosted, dedicated, private) and locale when applicable. Sampling rules: 60% Broad / 25% Safety-heavy / 15% Edge by default. Ensure per-cohort minimums in acceptance criteria. For A/B, allocate 50/50 traffic during each canary window unless otherwise approved.
regression_metrics: primary_metric: task_agreement_rate (example) - monitor absolute and relative changes
hallucination_rate - measured by automated reference-checker + spot human review
latency_p50 and latency_p95 - reported in ms
statistical_tests: Primary decision: two-sided t-test or bootstrap confidence interval depending on metric distribution; default alpha=0.01. Use sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) or alpha-spending across canary windows to avoid inflation. For multiple cohorts (locale/customer-tier), apply Benjamini-Hochberg to control FDR at q=0.05. Report MDE with assumed baseline variance; if MDE > observed effect, mark results Inconclusive. For safety signals with low base-rate, prefer exact binomial tests and require absolute delta thresholds (see acceptance criteria).
rollback_triggers: Immediate automatic rollback: any safety metric increase >0.25 percentage points absolute
Immediate manual halt (requires on-call and PM): safety increase between 0.10 and 0.25 pp, or any newly observed policy-violation class not seen in baseline
Automatic fail & reject promotion: primary metric degradation >= 0.75 pp absolute OR relative degradation >=1.5% while sample minimums met
Staged mitigation (manual): latency p95 increase >50ms and cost increase >10% with no primary improvement
Conditional rollback: consistent negative delta across 3 consecutive canary windows (1%, 3%, 10% traffic) for the same cohort
Emergency rollback override: SRE on-call may trigger rollback for infrastructure instability or cascading errors independent of metric thresholds
rollout_plan: Standard canary: 1% (sanity smoke) -> 10% (short window 1 hour or 1k interactions) -> 50% (24 hours) -> 100%. At each window run full eval suite. Use alpha spending for sequential testing. If canary passes, ramp continues; if a window fails, follow runbook. For Dedicated customers allow a 'reservation-mode' dry run with shadow traffic and no user-visible change. All canaries write to optimize-eval dashboard with real-time alerts to #optimize-canaries and paged alerts for safety thresholds.
runbook: 1) Alert fires to #optimize-canaries and on-call SRE. 2) Triage call within 15 minutes: PM, SRE, Eng on call, and data scientist. 3) Determine scope: safety vs performance vs cost. 4) If automatic rollback trigger met, provide rollback notice and execute immediate fallback. 5) Create GitHub PR with artifacts and preliminary analysis. 6) Follow-up post-mortem within 5 business days and create action items (bug fixes, promptset augmentation, model retraining).
